summary.tldr: Creates a national framework on cancers linked to firefighting and names January Firefighter Cancer Awareness Month.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to develop a national framework to raise awareness of cancers linked to firefighting and improve firefighters' access to prevention and treatment.
Requires the minister to consult provincial and territorial health officials, municipal governments, Indigenous governing bodies, health care professionals, scientists, and firefighting stakeholders.
Allows the framework to include research, training, screening, data collection, information sharing, and a summary of standards that treat these cancers as occupational diseases.
Requires the minister to table the framework in Parliament within one year after the Act comes into force and publish it on the Health Canada website.
Requires the minister to report within five years on the framework's effectiveness and on the state of prevention and treatment.
Designates January each year as Firefighter Cancer Awareness Month throughout Canada.
summary.background: The bill gives the Minister of Health the job of developing the framework and sets deadlines for a report to Parliament and a follow-up review. It also creates a yearly awareness month.
